submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires retrospectively on the word that states a comparison, a quantity or a degree - the 'how much / how many / how far / how likely' operator of a phrase, not the thing it describes: the comparative 'than' after a comparative adjective ('better than', 'more caution than courage'), set quantifiers that pick out an unspecified part of a set ('other', 'most', 'another', 'every', 'each', 'any', 'few', 'some', 'both', 'one of'), size/degree words ('small', 'little'), approximators ('about', 'nearly', 'hardly', 'almost', 'usually', 'largely'), epistemic possibility modals ('may', 'might') and the prepositions that place something relative to a reference point or a span ('between', 'among', 'within', 'during', 'throughout', 'near', 'beside', 'behind', 'under', 'beyond', 'towards'). It sits near its floor on content words and content-word heads ('house', 'lane', 'tall', 'long', 'great'), on exact numerals ('two', 'three', 'ten'), on demonstrative and possessive determiners ('this', 'that', 'his'), on contact/attachment prepositions ('with', 'on', 'of', 'in', 'along') and on coordinators ('and').

The cost of the repair came to three hundred and forty pounds, paid in part by the insurers and in part by the owners. The report closes with a note that the Alder sailed again in the spring and served on the same route until she was broken up in 1932. explanation_scores.explanation: The pole fires retrospectively on the word that states a comparison, a quantity or a degree - the 'how much / how many / how far / how likely' operator of a phrase, not the thing it describes: the comparative 'than' after a comparative adjective ('better than', 'more caution than courage'), set quantifiers that pick out an unspecified part of a set ('other', 'most', 'another', 'every', 'each', 'any', 'few', 'some', 'both', 'one of'), size/degree words ('small', 'little'), approximators ('about', 'nearly', 'hardly', 'almost', 'usually', 'largely'), epistemic possibility modals ('may', 'might') and the prepositions that place something relative to a reference point or a span ('between', 'among', 'within', 'during', 'throughout', 'near', 'beside', 'behind', 'under', 'beyond', 'towards'). It sits near its floor on content words and content-word heads ('house', 'lane', 'tall', 'long', 'great'), on exact numerals ('two', 'three', 'ten'), on demonstrative and possessive determiners ('this', 'that', 'his'), on contact/attachment prepositions ('with', 'on', 'of', 'in', 'along') and on coordinators ('and').
